newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Food to N.Korea may have been diverted to military.
newsitem.headline: Food to N.Korea may have been diverted to military.

text.p: U.S. congressmen returning from a visit to North Korea believe some foreign food aid might have been diverted to the communist state's military, one of them said on Wednesday.

Seven members of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, told a joint news conference in Seoul that they would seek steps to ensure that future U.S. aid to North Korea would go directly to hunger-stricken people.

"I believe we would all agree that some food aid has probably ended up in the hands of the military and the other elites in the country and we are concerned about that," California lawmaker Jane Harman said.
Harman, a Democrat, said the congressional delegation could see serious food problems in the impoverished nation and all members agreed that more aid was needed.

She said some aid officials the delegation interviewed in North Korea "confirmed that some food is reaching the people". Other congressmen said the North did not allow them to monitor distribution of food aid.
"In terms of future U.S. aid we made clear that we need assurance that that aid go directly to the people who most need it," Harman said.
